$comment: Startup import budget (parent AC1, WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B). Ratchet: a module added to the static import graph of src/cli.ts (or to the fast path's dynamic-import set, or its runtime module union) fails tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts; regenerate deliberately with `npm run benchmark:wl-startup -- --target <src|dist> --update-budget` (removals are improvements and must be recorded the same way).

ac1Targets.note: Parent AC1 target (p95 wall <= 700 ms, peak RSS <= 68 MB on a warm cache hit), accepted at the measured dist floor on the reference host per the producer decision on WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B (2026-10-21): the F7 slimmed fast path (4 static modules, 3 dynamic entries gated behind the --version branch) measured dist p95 689 ms wall / 630 ms CPU / 67.8 MB RSS for `wl next --json`, 645 / 607 / 67.9 MB for `wl list --status open --json`, and 547 / 492 / 60.9 MB for `wl --version`, against a bare-node floor of 484 ms / 458 ms CPU / 61.2 MB on the same (loaded) host. `enforced` is true per that decision: the measured floors are within the accepted target (the original 500 ms / 60 MB budget sat at or below the bare-node floor and was unreachable by import slimming alone).

regression.note: Sample statistic: the measured assertions use the median (`statistic: "p50"`) of 7 samples, not a p95 over four — a p95 over four samples is the maximum of four, the jumpiest possible estimator, and it failed the dev-push gate on unchanged code when the host was busy (WL-0MWIF616V008380O spawned a duplicate triage item; WL-0MWHUMOHJ006ZMBQ lost several otherwise-good child worktrees to it). A median over an odd sample count is a real sample: one contended outlier cannot decide the verdict, while a genuine regression moves every sample and still fails (pinned by the AC4 anti-blunting tests). The recorded baselines stay p95 values — re-recording them belongs with per-host-class baselines this repository does not own — so the unchanged headroom percentages remain the effective margin, because the measured spread puts the median and the p95 within a few percent of each other. Root cause of the RSS flake (WL-0MWIGCK0E009GGLG, measured): `tsx` loads a per-user cache from `$TMPDIR/tsx-<uid>` at startup, so an inherited TMPDIR pointing at a long-lived scratch tree (the test harness uses a shared 4.3 GB directory with a 354 MB / 32k-entry `tsx-1000/` cache) inflated the same `wl --version` from ~96 MiB to 129-133 MiB on unchanged code. The benchmark now pins the measured child's TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP (`buildBenchmarkChildEnv`) to a fresh benchmark-owned directory, and the measured suite runs in its own serialised vitest project after the rest of the suite (`startup-budget-measured`: `maxWorkers: 1`, `sequence.groupOrder: 1`). CPU time (process.resourceUsage user+system, from the F1 spawn records) is the load-independent regression gate, with 100 % headroom because the `src` (tsx) target's CPU time varies ~50 % run-to-run on a shared host (transpile + frequency/cache effects: an F7 gate run measured 3226 ms against a 2149 ms baseline's 50 % limit of 3224 ms). Wall time gets 200 % + a 250 ms floor and is additionally normalised by the host-load factor measured by that run's bare-node control (measured floor / recorded floor, clamped at `maxHostLoadFactor` = 8, never below 1), so a saturated host cannot flake the ratchet (WL-0MVS9Z965006MC4R: warm cache-hit wall at 7512.9 ms vs the un-normalised 6903 ms limit while CPU stayed flat). Peak RSS keeps a tighter 25 % headroom (`rssHeadroomPct`) so memory regressions still fail promptly, and its recorded budget is normalised by the SAME bare-node host-load factor as wall time (WL-0MWIGNGP3001O7HP: memory pressure from concurrent full suites inflated peak RSS ~26 % on byte-identical code — 132.4 MiB vs a 132.4 MiB limit from a 105.9 MiB baseline — so RSS now scales with the host like wall time does; upward-only, pinned by test). A genuine CPU regression (doubling) still fails; the AC1 target is asserted separately once `ac1Targets.enforced`.

src.method: /usr/bin/node node_modules/.bin/tsx src/cli.ts <scenario argv> — warm runs after a cold-start warmup; CPU/RSS from the F1 spawn records (WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE)

dist.method: /usr/bin/node dist/cli.js <scenario argv> — warm runs after a cold-start warmup; CPU/RSS from the F1 spawn records (WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE)
